(1) we present a new meta-reinforcement algorithm that is both extrapolates well to out-of-distribution data, and is efficient, requiring only a few thousand samples per task for on-policy meta-reinforcement training, (2) our approach uses a dynamics model, and (3) we demonstrate that our algorithm can learn to solve complex tasks with a single meta-reinforcement step.

(1) meta-training a dynamics model is a more efficient way to learn a prior than meta-training a policy or value function, and (2) using this dynamics model to generate synthetic experience for off-policy training of a policy can be a more efficient way of learning a new policy than on-policy meta-reinforcement training, especially when there is a distributional shift
